issues.legal_issue: The permission mechanism for prosecuting registration offences does not bar a private person from commencing a prosecution without permission.
material_facts: A private complainant alleged that the accused conspired to forge a lease and register it using false personation.

The trial court acquitted the appellant, but the High Court convicted him of abetting an offence under the registration law after finding that he identified the person falsely appearing before the Sub-Registrar.
The appellant argued that the private complaint was incompetent because the complainant had not obtained the permission specified in the registration law.
The appeal before the Supreme Court raised only the competency of the complaint on that ground.
issues.conclusion: The complaint was not barred for want of permission, and the appeal was dismissed.
issues.legal_principle: Section 83(1) of the Indian Registration Act, 1908, applies to prosecutions for offences under the Act that come to a registering officer’s knowledge in that officer’s official capacity. It permissively enables the specified officials to commence or authorize a prosecution; it does not prohibit a private person from prosecuting, even where the officer has such knowledge. The Court approved Gopinath v. Kuldip Singh, Re Piranu Nadathi, and Emperor v. Yesa Nath Didiwagh; it disapproved Nge Pan Gaing v. King Emperor and Emperor v. Mohd. Mehdi. Ganga Dibya v. Emperor and Habib Shah v. Mehda Shah were referred to. K. M. Kanavi v. State of Mysore was inapplicable because the provision considered there used different language. By contrast, section 195(1) of the Code of Criminal Procedure, section 70(1) of the Indian Stamp Act, and section 29 of the Indian Arms Act, 1878, use prohibitory language.

predicates.registration_offence_prosecution: The proceeding is a prosecution for an offence under the registration law.
predicates.private_person_complaint: A private person commences the prosecution by complaint.
predicates.permission_not_obtained: The private complainant commences the prosecution without obtaining permission from the specified registration officials.

issues.definition: When a private person complains of a registration-law offence without obtaining the specified officials’ permission, the prosecution is not barred for that reason.
